Q30.text: we further examine the phenomenological framework of educational VR platforms
Q30.source: King & Salvo (2023), Physiological Assessment of Learning in VR Clinical Immersion (P1), ASEE Paper #37129
Q30.locus: unpaginated (ASEE); END OF INTRODUCTION, immediately before Methods — verified not the abstract

Q31.text: Boredom is the aversive experience of having an unfulfilled desire to be engaged in satisfying activity
Q31.source: Fahlman, Shelley A., Kimberley B. Mercer-Lynn, David B. Flora, and John D. Eastwood, Development and Validation of the Multidimensional State Boredom Scale (2013), Assessment 20(1): 68-85
Q31.locus: printed p. 69 (folio-read: page-69 header follows the corresponding-author block; the page-70 header falls two sentences later)
Q31.use: L1 P1 footnote — the definition our 2023 study adopted, cited to ITS OWN SOURCE per author ruling, not to the paper that adopted it
Q31.caveat: Full-sentence form, so a colon introduction keeps the capital legitimately. Fahlman offers it as a TRANSTHEORETICAL definition — the common core of existing theories rather than one theory among them, which is what licensed its downstream adoption as neutral. Q05 is the same definition as a lowercase fragment.

Q32.text: Attunements are something that cannot be straightforwardly ascertained in a universally valid way, like a fact that we could lead everyone to see
Q32.source: Heidegger, The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics; printed p. 65 (running head; archon records pp.62-63 = PDF pages of a TWO-PAGE SPREAD)
Q32.use: L1 - the sentence PRECEDING Q22; states the claim Q22 then sharpens

Q33.text: For all ascertaining means bringing to consciousness
Q33.source: Heidegger, The Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics; printed p. 65 (running head; archon records pp.62-63 = PDF pages of a TWO-PAGE SPREAD)
Q33.use: L1 - THE HINGE that makes Q23 intelligible: ascertaining = bringing to consciousness, which is why making conscious alters the attunement
